claim: The unfolded protein response (UPR) drives transcriptional programs in all organisms analyzed to date that allow cells to cope with ER stress.
source_text: In all organisms analyzed to date, the UPR drives transcriptional programs that allow cells to cope with ER stress.
evidence_reasoning: This statement reflects established scientific consensus about UPR function across organisms prior to the findings of this study.

claim: The non-conventional splicing of Hac1 (yeasts) and XBP1 (metazoans) mRNA is conserved and dependent on Ire1.
source_text: The non-conventional splicing of Hac1 (yeasts) and XBP1 (metazoans) mRNA, encoding orthologous UPR transcription activators, is conserved and dependent on Ire1, an ER membrane-resident kinase/endoribonuclease.
evidence_reasoning: This represents established knowledge in the field about conserved UPR mechanisms, supported by prior literature.

claim: Schizosaccharomyces pombe lacks both a Hac1/XBP1 ortholog and a UPR-dependent-transcriptional-program.
source_text: We found that the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe lacks both a Hac1/XBP1 ortholog and a UPR-dependent-transcriptional-program.
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding based on experimental observations and genomic analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Ire1 initiates the selective decay of a subset of ER-localized-mRNAs that is required to survive ER stress in S. pombe.
source_text: Instead, Ire1 initiates the selective decay of a subset of ER-localized-mRNAs that is required to survive ER stress.
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data including RNA-seq and viability assays presented in the manuscript.

claim: Bip1 mRNA is the sole mRNA cleaved upon Ire1 activation that escapes decay in S. pombe.
source_text: We identified Bip1 mRNA, encoding a major ER-chaperone, as the sole mRNA cleaved upon Ire1 activation that escapes decay.
evidence_reasoning: This finding is supported by Northern blot analysis, RNA-seq data, and 3' RACE experiments presented in the manuscript.

claim: Truncation of Bip1 mRNA's 3′ UTR, including loss of its polyA tail, stabilizes Bip1 mRNA.
source_text: Instead, truncation of its 3′ UTR, including loss of its polyA tail, stabilized Bip1 mRNA, resulting in increased Bip1 translation.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data including Northern blots, mRNA half-life measurements, and ribosome profiling presented in the manuscript.

claim: Truncation of Bip1 mRNA results in increased Bip1 translation.
source_text: Instead, truncation of its 3′ UTR, including loss of its polyA tail, stabilized Bip1 mRNA, resulting in increased Bip1 translation.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by ribosome profiling and polysome analysis data presented in Figure 4.

claim: S. pombe uses a universally conserved stress-sensing machinery in novel ways to maintain homeostasis in the ER.
source_text: Thus, S. pombe uses a universally conserved stress-sensing machinery in novel ways to maintain homeostasis in the ER.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings showing that S. pombe uses Ire1 differently than other organisms.

claim: ER stress is toxic to cells and triggers cell death when unmitigated.
source_text: When unmitigated, ER stress is toxic to cells and triggers cell death
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citations to Shore et al., 2011; Tabas and Ron, 2011; Hetz, 2012.

claim: Three ER-resident transmembrane sensors (Ire1, PERK, ATF6) transmit information into the cytosol in metazoan cells.
source_text: In metazoan cells, three ER-resident transmembrane sensors, Ire1, PERK, ATF6 transmit information into the cytosol.
evidence_reasoning: This represents established knowledge about metazoan UPR pathways, supported by citation to Walter and Ron, 2011.

claim: Ire1 is a bifunctional transmembrane kinase/endoribonuclease.
source_text: Ire1 is a bifunctional transmembrane kinase/endoribonuclease that controls expression of the transcription factor XBP1 by a non-conventional splicing of its mRNA.
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about Ire1's enzymatic activities.

claim: Ire1 uses its ER-lumenal domain to detect unfolded proteins.
source_text: Ire1 uses its ER-lumenal domain to detect unfolded proteins, and in response activates by homo-oligomerization, trans-autophosphorylation, and allosteric activation of its cytosolic nuclease modality
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citations to Korennykh et al., 2009; Gardner and Walter, 2011.

claim: Activated Ire1 cleaves XBP1 mRNA at two discrete stem-loop structures, excising a short intron.
source_text: Activated Ire1 cleaves the XBP1 mRNA at two discrete stem-loop structures, excising a short intron.
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about XBP1 mRNA splicing, supported by citations to Yoshida et al., 2001; Calfon et al., 2002.

claim: Ire1 was first discovered in the budding yeast S. cerevisiae.
source_text: Ire1 was first discovered in the budding yeast S. cerevisiae, where it constitutes the core machinery of the cells' only UPR signaling pathway
evidence_reasoning: This is historical knowledge supported by citations to Cox et al., 1993; Mori et al., 1993.

claim: S. cerevisiae Ire1 splices Hac1 mRNA by a mechanism conserved in all metazoan cells.
source_text: S. cerevisiae Ire1 splices Hac1 mRNA, encoding the yeast ortholog of XBP1, by a mechanism that was later found conserved in all metazoan cells
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citations to Cox and Walter, 1996; Sidrauski et al., 1996.

claim: Ire1-mediated mRNA splicing is the most evolutionary ancient branch of the UPR.
source_text: Ire1-mediated mRNA splicing therefore is considered to be the most evolutionary ancient branch of the UPR.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion based on evolutionary conservation patterns established in the literature.

claim: PERK reduces the load of proteins entering the ER through translational control.
source_text: PERK superimposes another layer of control by reducing the load of proteins entering the ER through translational control
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about PERK function, supported by citation to Pavitt and Ron, 2012.

claim: Ire1 induction in Drosophila cells results in both splicing of XBP1 mRNA and enhanced mRNA breakdown.
source_text: In particular, Hollien and Weissman (2006) first discovered in Drosophila cells that Ire1 induction not only results in splicing of XBP1 mRNA but also mediates enhanced mRNA breakdown.
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from prior work, supported by citation to Hollien and Weissman, 2006.

claim: Regulated Ire1-dependent decay (RIDD) is conserved in mammalian cells but not in S. cerevisiae.
source_text: This output of Ire1 activation, termed 'regulated Ire1-dependent decay' (RIDD), is conserved in mammalian cells, but not in S. cerevisiae
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citations to Niwa et al., 2005; Han et al., 2009; Hollien et al., 2009.

claim: All identified RIDD target mRNAs are translated by membrane-bound ribosomes at the ER surface.
source_text: All identified RIDD target mRNAs are translated by membrane-bound ribosomes at the ER surface, where they are cleaved, most likely by Ire1 directly
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citations to Han et al., 2009; Hollien et al., 2009; Cross et al., 2012.

claim: RIDD target mRNAs do not contain easily recognizable features in common.
source_text: By contrast to the strictly conserved stem/loop structures found at Hac1/XBP1 mRNA splice sites (Gonzalez et al., 1999), RIDD target mRNAs do not contain easily recognizable features in common.
evidence_reasoning: This is a comparison to established knowledge about splice site conservation, with citation to Gonzalez et al., 1999.

claim: RIDD cleavage reactions have been reconstituted in vitro with recombinantly expressed purified Ire1.
source_text: RIDD cleavage reactions have been reconstituted in vitro with recombinantly expressed purified Ire1, lending support to the notion that Ire1's endoribonuclease actvity, rather than another enzyme recruited to it, carries out the initial cleavage reaction
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Lee et al., 2011; Cross et al., 2012.

claim: RIDD contributes to important feedback control on proinsulin expression in pancreatic beta-cells.
source_text: RIDD has been suggested to play cytoprotective roles, such as contributing to important feedback control on proinsulin expression in pancreatic beta-cells
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Lipson et al., 2008.

claim: RIDD protects liver cells from acetaminophen toxicity by degrading mRNAs encoding cytochrome P450 variants.
source_text: RIDD has been suggested to play cytoprotective roles, such as...protecting liver cells from acetaminophen toxicity by degrading the mRNAs encoding the cytochrome P450 variants responsible for the drug's toxification
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Hur et al., 2012.

claim: RIDD is a major contributor driving cells into apoptosis after prolonged and unmitigated exposure to ER stress.
source_text: RIDD has also been suggested to play cytotoxic roles as a major contributor driving cells into apoptosis after prolonged and unmitigated exposure to ER stress
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Han et al., 2009.

claim: There is no evidence that Ire1 controls transcription in the UPR of S. pombe.
source_text: Surprisingly, in the work presented here we found no evidence that Ire1 controls transcription in the UPR of Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding based on RNA-seq data showing no UPR-dependent transcriptional upregulation.

claim: S. pombe Ire1 maintains ER homeostasis through two post-transcriptional mechanisms.
source_text: Instead, in S. pombe Ire1 maintains ER homeostasis through two post-transcriptional mechanisms: it initiates RIDD of a large, select set of ER-targeted mRNAs and processes Bip1 mRNA in an unprecedented way, thereby stabilizing it.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion based on experimental findings including RNA-seq, Northern blots, and functional assays.

claim: Ire1Δ and Ire1(H1018N) mutant cells show reduced viability on ER stress-inducing media.
source_text: Viability assay by serial dilution of wild type, Ire1Δ and Ire1(H1018N) cells spotted on solid media with or without 0.03 µg/ml of the ER stress inducer tunicamycin (Tm).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the viability assay data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: Thirty-nine mRNA species were reduced by more than twofold in a DTT- and Ire1-dependent manner in S. pombe.
source_text: Thirty-nine mRNA species were reduced by more than twofold in a DTT- and Ire1-dependent manner
evidence_reasoning: This is based on RNA-seq analysis presented in Figure 1c.

claim: The set of down-regulated genes exclusively encoded proteins targeted to the ER.
source_text: Intriguingly, the set of down-regulated genes exclusively encoded proteins targeted to the ER (identified by signal sequences and/or transmembrane segments)
evidence_reasoning: This is based on RNA-seq data combined with bioinformatic analysis of protein targeting signals.

claim: More than half of the most down-regulated mRNAs encode proteins with annotated functions in the secretory pathway.
source_text: More than half of the most down-regulated mRNAs encode proteins with annotated functions in the secretory pathway, in particular proteins involved in lipid metabolism, trafficking, and ER functions
evidence_reasoning: This is based on gene ontology analysis of RNA-seq data presented in Figure 1e.

claim: Gas2 mRNA shows Ire1-dependent cleavage products that accumulate in Ski2Δ cells.
source_text: Northern blot of total RNA extracted from wild type, Ire1Δ, Ski2Δ and double mutant ER stressed Ire1Δ Ski2Δ cells (2 mM DTT, 1 hr). A probe complementary to the 5′ UTR of Gas2 was used to detect cleavage products.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by Northern blot data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: Ski2 is required for degradation of Ire1-cleaved mRNA fragments.
source_text: To this end, we sought to trap any putative primary Ire1-cleavage products prior to degradation by deleting...Ski2Δ mutant strains impaired in exosome function
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the experimental design and the accumulation of cleavage products in Ski2Δ cells shown in Figure 2.

claim: Ire1-dependent cleavage sites in S. pombe contain a core motif with three conserved nucleotides (UG\C).
source_text: Alignment of the experimentally determined Ire1-dependent cleavage sites revealed a core motif with a signature of three conserved nucleotides (UG\C) that flank the Ire1-dependent cleavage sites at positions −2, −1, and +1
evidence_reasoning: This is based on 3' end mapping and sequence analysis presented in Figure 2e.

claim: The information contained within the Gas2 ORF is sufficient to confer susceptibility to Ire1-dependent cleavage.
source_text: Indeed, a Gas2 reporter construct transcribed off a heterologous alpha-tubulin (Nda2) promoter and containing only the Gas2 ORF flanked by heterologous 5′ and 3′ tubulin untranslated regions (UTRs), was down-regulated upon ER stress in an Ire1-dependent manner...indicating that the information contained within the Gas2 ORF is sufficient to confer susceptibility to Ire1-dependent cleavage.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by qPCR data of the reporter construct shown in Figure 2f.

claim: Mutation of the UGC-residues at the Gas2 mRNA cleavage site abolishes ER stress-dependent cleavage at that site.
source_text: To assess the functional importance of the identified Gas2 mRNA cleavage site experimentally, we mutated the UGC-residues of the ▲-site (UG\CU). As expected, ER stress-dependent cleavage of the Gas2 reporter mRNA at the mapped site was abolished
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by Northern blot data of the mutant construct shown in Figure 2g.

claim: Ire1-dependent mRNA cleavage in S. pombe is sequence dependent.
source_text: Taken together, we conclude that Ire1-dependent mRNA cleavage in S. pombe is sequence dependent.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is based on mutational analysis and sequence motif identification presented in Figure 2.

claim: Bip1 mRNA abundance increases approximately fourfold upon ER stress in wild type cells.
source_text: Northern blot analysis of total RNA extracted from wild type and Ire1Δ cells untreated or treated with tunicamycin (1 µg/ml), and hybridized with a probe complementary to the ORF of Bip1 mRNA. Right panel: quantitation normalized to Pgk1 mRNA.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by Northern blot quantitation shown in Figure 3a.

claim: Bip1 mRNA processing is dependent on Ire1.
source_text: Northern blot analysis of total RNA extracted from wild type and Ire1Δ cells untreated or treated with tunicamycin
evidence_reasoning: This is shown by the absence of processed Bip1 mRNA in Ire1Δ cells in Figure 3a.

claim: A GFP mRNA driven by the Bip1 promoter does not show the same increase in abundance as endogenous Bip1 mRNA upon ER stress.
source_text: The abundance of a GFP mRNA driven by the Bip1 promoter (black) compared to endogenous Bip1 mRNA was determined as a time course after DTT (2 mM) addition by quantitative Northern blotting.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the data shown in Figure 3b, indicating post-transcriptional regulation.

claim: Truncated Bip1 mRNA (tBip1) is more stable than full-length Bip1 mRNA.
source_text: Wild type cells bearing a construct encoding the Nmt1 5′ UTR, Bip1 ORF and Bip1 3′ UTR driven by the Nmt1 promoter were pre-treated with tunicamycin (0.25 µg/ml, 1 hr). At different time points after thiamine (15 µM) addition (to effect transcriptional shut-off of the Nmt1 promoter), RNA was extracted and analyzed by Northern hybridization.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by mRNA half-life measurements shown in Figure 3c.

claim: tBip1 mRNA lacks a polyA tail and terminates at G373 in the 3′ UTR.
source_text: The sequence of the amplified DNA confirmed that tBip1 mRNA lacks a polyA tail and terminates at G373 in the 3′ UTR
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by 3' RACE sequencing data presented in Figure 3d.

claim: The sequences flanking G373 in Bip1 mRNA align with the UG\CU motif.
source_text: The sequences flanking G373 align with the UG\CU motif (Figure 2e), suggesting that tBip1 mRNA is produced by truncation of Bip1 mRNA in an Ire1-dependent RNA cleavage reaction
evidence_reasoning: This is based on sequence analysis comparing the Bip1 cleavage site to the consensus motif.

claim: Mutation of G373 to C or U and its deletion abolishes Ire1-dependent Bip1 mRNA processing.
source_text: Mutation of G373 to C or U and its deletion together with preceding nucleotides abolished Ire1-dependent Bip1 mRNA processing
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by mutational analysis shown in Figure 3e.

claim: Bip1 mRNA is the only stable mRNA in S. pombe that loses its polyA tail upon UPR induction.
source_text: From these data we conclude that, remarkably, Bip1 mRNA is the only stable mRNA in the cell that loses its polyA tail upon UPR induction.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is based on comparison of polyA+ and total RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3f.

claim: tBip1 mRNA is associated with polyribosomes.
source_text: Northern blot analysis of the distribution of total or tBip1 mRNA in polyribosomes from extracts of unstressed or ER-stressed (2 mM DTT, 1 hr) cells.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by polysome fractionation data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: tBip1 mRNA is translated.
source_text: tBip1 mRNA is translated and is important for fitness during ER stress.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by ribosome footprinting data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: Cells carrying a deletion of Bip1 mRNA cleavage sites show a marked growth delay after ER stress.
source_text: Liquid cultures of Bip1 mRNA mutant, that were exposed to a pulse of ER stress (tunicamycin) and allowed to recover after washout of the drug showed a marked growth delay in early log phase
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by growth curve data shown in Figure 4c.

claim: Cells carrying a deletion of Bip1 mRNA cleavage sites show enhanced cell death after ER stress.
source_text: Liquid cultures of Bip1 mRNA mutant, that were exposed to a pulse of ER stress (tunicamycin) and allowed to recover after washout of the drug showed...enhanced cell death
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by colony forming unit assay data shown in Figure 4d.

claim: Bip1 mRNA processing is important for maintaining cell fitness in the face of ER stress.
source_text: indicating that Bip1 mRNA processing is important for maintaining cell fitness in the face of ER stress.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is based on the growth and viability defects observed in Bip1 cleavage site mutants.

claim: The importance of Bip1 mRNA processing varies with growth conditions.
source_text: By contrast to cell growth in liquid culture, Bip1 mutant cells grew on UPR-inducing tunicamycin plates only marginally worse that wild type cells...The importance of Bip1 mRNA processing, therefore, varies with growth conditions.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on comparing liquid culture growth data with plate growth assays.

claim: RIDD reduces the total protein influx into the ER by only 15% in S. pombe under severe ER stress conditions.
source_text: Indeed, a back-of-the-envelope calculation indicates that in S. pombe RIDD reduces the total protein influx into the ER by only 15%, even under the severe ER stress conditions explored here experimentally.
evidence_reasoning: This is calculated from ribosome footprinting data analyzing translational engagement of ER-targeted mRNAs.

claim: mRNAs encoding proteins involved in lipid metabolism are highly enriched among RIDD targets.
source_text: In support of this notion, we notice that the population of RIDD target mRNAs is highly selective. mRNAs encoding proteins involved in lipid metabolism are highly enriched (31% of RIDD target mRNA as compared to 6.7% in all ER-targeted mRNAs).
evidence_reasoning: This is based on gene ontology analysis of RIDD target mRNAs shown in Figure 1e.

claim: RIDD targets encoding proteins involved in sterol metabolism are particularly enriched.
source_text: Moreover, we find that RIDD targets encoding proteins involved in sterol metabolism are particularly enriched (13% as compared to 1.3%).
evidence_reasoning: This is based on gene ontology analysis of RIDD target mRNAs.

claim: Ire1 is the nuclease that initiates RIDD in metazoan cells.
source_text: Previous work strongly suggests that Ire1 is the nuclease that initiates RIDD in metazoan cells
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Han et al., 2009; Hollien et al., 2009; Cross et al., 2012.

claim: An Ire1 RNase active site mutant, Ire1(H1018N), is unable to sustain cell growth on ER stress-inducing media.
source_text: we show that an Ire1 RNase active site mutant, Ire1(H1018N), is unable to sustain cell growth on ER stress-inducing media.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by viability assay data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: Cleaved RIDD target mRNAs carry a 2′,3′-cyclic phosphate group.
source_text: Second, we showed that cleaved RIDD target mRNAs carry a 2′,3′-cyclic phosphate group, which is a prerequisite for the ligation reaction (tRNA ligase) used in the genome-wide mapping of mRNA ends created upon ER stress.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by the successful ligation of linkers using tRNA ligase, which specifically requires 2',3'-cyclic phosphates.

claim: Ire1 and tRNA endonuclease are the only cytoplasmic nucleases known to produce 2′,3′-cyclic phosphate products.
source_text: Ire1 and tRNA endonuclease (and the Ire1-family member RNase L found in mammalian cells) are the only cytoplasmic nucleases known to produce such products.
evidence_reasoning: This represents established knowledge about nuclease activities and their products.

claim: In S. cerevisiae, Ire1 has a single known substrate, Hac1 mRNA.
source_text: In S. cerevisiae, Ire1 has a single known substrate, Hac1 mRNA
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Niwa et al., 2005.

claim: Hac1 and XBP1 mRNA have highly conserved stem loop structures that demarcate the splice sites.
source_text: Hac1 and XBP1 mRNA have highly conserved and readily recognizable stem loop structures that demarcate the splice sites.
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Gonzalez et al., 1999.

claim: Cleavage of Hac1/XBP1 mRNA occurs at a universally conserved G at position 3 in the seven-base loop.
source_text: Cleavage occurs at a universally conserved G always found at position 3 in the seven-base loop
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Gonzalez et al., 1999.

claim: Constructs derived from S. cerevisiae Hac1 mRNA are properly spliced in mammalian cells.
source_text: This information is interchangeable between species: constructs derived from S. cerevisiae Hac1 mRNA are properly spliced in mammalian cells
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Niwa et al., 1999.

claim: Yeast Ire1 recognizes and precisely cleaves XBP1 mRNA-derived substrates.
source_text: yeast Ire1 recognizes and precisely cleaves XBP1 mRNA-derived substrates
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Niwa et al., 1999.

claim: RIDD target mRNAs contain a short three-base UGC consensus at the Ire1 cleavage site where cleavage occurs after the G.
source_text: We show that RIDD target mRNAs contain a short three-base UGC consensus at the Ire1 cleavage site where cleavage occurs after the G
evidence_reasoning: This is based on sequence analysis of mapped cleavage sites shown in Figure 2e.

claim: UGC triplets occur much more frequently in mRNAs than Ire1 cleavage sites.
source_text: By chance, UGC triplets occur much more frequently in mRNAs than Ire1 cleavage sites.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the observation that only specific UGC sites are cleaved despite many being present in the genome.

claim: Many identified cleavage sites lie in loops of potential hairpin structures.
source_text: We and others note that many of the identified cleavage sites lie in loops of potential hairpin structures
evidence_reasoning: This is based on structural analysis of cleavage sites, with citation to Hur et al., 2012; Oikawa et al., 2010.

claim: Mutation of one cleavage site in Gas2 mRNA gives rise to cleavage at alternative sites.
source_text: The concept of Ire1 recruitment, whether through interactions via the nascent chain or elements in the mRNA per se, is supported by our finding that mutation of one cleavage site (UG\C → UC\U) in Gas2 mRNA gives rise to cleavage at alternative sites.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by Northern blot data of the mutant construct shown in Figure 2g.

claim: Clearance of Ire1-cleavage products by Ski2 may be a requirement for continued Ire1 activity.
source_text: This kinetic behavior suggests that clearance of Ire1-cleavage products by Ski2 may be a requirement for continued Ire1 activity.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative interpretation of the transient accumulation of cleavage products in Ski2Δ cells.

claim: S. pombe Bip1 mRNA changes size upon ER stress, an observation dating back to 1992.
source_text: The observation that S. pombe Bip1 mRNA changes size upon ER stress dates back to 1992
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Pidoux and Armstrong, 1992.

claim: Bip1 mRNA processing has not been observed in any species other than S. pombe.
source_text: To date, Bip1 mRNA processing has not been observed in any other species.
evidence_reasoning: This represents the state of knowledge in the field based on literature review.

claim: A plausible explanation for the increased stability of tBip1 mRNA is the loss of an RNA degron located in the severed portion of the 3′ UTR.
source_text: A plausible explanation for the increased stability of tBip1 mRNA is the loss of an RNA degron located in the severed portion of the 3′ UTR.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative explanation for the observed stability increase.

claim: Histone mRNAs lack polyA tails and provide precedence for stable, translatable mRNAs without polyA tails.
source_text: Although polyA tails are generally linked to stability and translational efficiency, histone mRNAs, which likewise lack polyA tails, provide precedence for such an exception to the rule
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Marzluff et al., 2008.

claim: Histone mRNAs terminate in a well-conserved 3′ stem-loop structure that protects from exonucleolytic degradation.
source_text: Histone mRNAs terminate in a well-conserved 3′ stem-loop structure, which protects from exonucleolytic degradation.
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Sanchez and Marzluff, 2002.

claim: A predicted conserved hairpin structure exists at the 3′ termini of tBip1 RNAs in some fission yeasts.
source_text: Indeed, we find a predicted conserved hairpin structure at the 3′ termini of tBip1 RNAs in some fission yeasts (S. pombe, S. octosporus and S. cryophilus)
evidence_reasoning: This is based on computational prediction of RNA secondary structure.

claim: Preliminary mutational analysis failed to validate the importance of the predicted hairpin structure for mRNA stability in S. pombe.
source_text: however preliminary mutational analysis failed to validate its importance for mRNA stability in S. pombe.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on unpublished mutational experiments mentioned in the text.

claim: Bip1 mRNA is the only mRNA in S. pombe in the expressed genome that is subject to this unique regulation.
source_text: Our data show that Bip1 mRNA is the only mRNA in S. pombe in the expressed genome that is subject to this unique regulation.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on genome-wide RNA-seq analysis comparing polyA+ and total RNA.

claim: Bip1 is the most pleiotropically important and precisely controlled ER chaperone based on work in other species.
source_text: From work in other species, Bip1 emerges as the most pleiotropically important and precisely controlled ER chaperone
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Gulow et al., 2002.

claim: Bip1 holds a unique position in S. pombe where it is glycosylated.
source_text: Moreover, Bip1 holds a unique position in S. pombe, where it is glycosylated
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Pidoux and Armstrong, 1993.

claim: Ire1 in S. pombe clusters tightly with enzymes involved in the quality control cycle of glycosylated proteins in gene interaction maps.
source_text: A recent comprehensive gene interaction map revealed that Ire1 in S. pombe clusters tightly with enzymes involved in the quality control cycle of glycosylated proteins
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Frost et al., 2012.

claim: In S. cerevisiae, E-maps confirm the linear relationship between Ire1 and Hac1.
source_text: By contrast, corresponding E-maps in S. cerevisiae succinctly confirm the long-appreciated linear relationship between Ire1 and Hac1
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Schuldiner et al., 2005.

claim: The UPR in S. pombe provides an example of how molecular machines can be repurposed evolutionarily.
source_text: From an evolutionary angle, the UPR in S. pombe provides an intriguing example of how molecular machines can be repurposed.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conceptual conclusion drawn from the comparative analysis of UPR mechanisms across species.

claim: In S. cerevisiae, folding capacity is increased via transcriptional up-regulation during the UPR.
source_text: In S. cerevisiae, folding capacity is increased via transcriptional up-regulation
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about the S. cerevisiae UPR mechanism.

claim: In S. pombe, the folding load is decreased and the ER is restructured during the UPR.
source_text: in S. pombe the folding load is decreased and the ER is restructured.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion based on the experimental findings of RIDD and Bip1 regulation.

claim: In metazoan cells, both modes of Ire1 activity (transcriptional and RIDD) are merged.
source_text: In metazoan cells, both modes of Ire1 activity are merged, and depending on condition and cell type can serve different purposes.
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about metazoan UPR mechanisms.

claim: RIDD can protect insulin secreting cells by removing major secretory protein loads.
source_text: RIDD can protect cells by removing major secretory protein loads, as it is the case in insulin secreting cells
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Lipson et al., 2008.

claim: RIDD can serve to activate apoptotic pathways in cells experiencing prolonged and unmitigated ER stress.
source_text: or it can serve to activate apopototic pathways, as it is the case in cells experiencing prolonged and unmitigated ER stress
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Han et al., 2009.

claim: A primitive UPR may have served primarily as an ER-localized yet promiscuous RNA degradation system.
source_text: it is tempting to speculate that a broader mRNA degradation pathway preceded the development of the more specialized splicing mechanism...a primitive UPR may have served primarily as an ER-localized yet promiscuous RNA degradation system.
evidence_reasoning: This is explicitly presented as speculation about evolutionary origins.

claim: The stem/loop splice sites of HAC1/XBP1 mRNAs could be the result of a long time optimization process.
source_text: In this way, the stem/loop splice sites of HAC1/XBP1 mRNAs could be the result of a long time optimization process
evidence_reasoning: This is explicitly presented as speculation about evolutionary development.

claim: S. cerevisiae emerges as the endpoint of an optimization process rather than an evolutionary precursor.
source_text: In this view, S. cerevisiae emerges as the endpoint of an optimization process rather than an evolutionary precursor.
evidence_reasoning: This is explicitly presented as a speculative evolutionary interpretation.
